## [Node.js Backend: Hexagonal Architecture](../05-building-block-view/node.md)

- NODE-ARCH-01: New backends use this layout.
- NODE-ARCH-02: `src/platform` holds what several contexts share, in the same rings: `platform/domain` (error base classes, `Caller`, shared value objects;
- NODE-ARCH-03: Contexts import each other only through `index.ts` (ARCH-ORG-09).
- NODE-ARCH-04: `domain` imports only its own ring and `src/platform/domain/index.ts`; `ports` and `application` also their own rings, `src/platform/ports/index.ts` and zod (ARCH-DEP-02/03).
- NODE-ARCH-05: Ports return `Promise` and may take an `AbortSignal` (NODE-D4).
- NODE-ARCH-06: Commands and queries are immutable and created only through a factory that validates with a zod schema next to them in `ports/in` (ARCH-UC-05/06).
- NODE-ARCH-07: Each error category of ARCH-UC-13 has one class in `src/platform/domain`:
- NODE-ARCH-08: Domain types are `readonly`.
- NODE-ARCH-09: The adapter maps; the core never sees transport types (ARCH-MAP-).
- NODE-ARCH-10: Nothing blocks the event loop.
- NODE-ARCH-11: Every promise is awaited or explicitly handled.
- NODE-ARCH-12: `process.env` is read only in `src/platform/config` (configuration/nestjs.md).
- NODE-ARCH-13: dependency-cruiser checks the rings in CI (ARCH-ENF-01, NODE-D8) with `tsPreCompilationDeps: true`, so type-only imports count.
- NODE-ARCH-14: Guard against "checks nothing" (ARCH-ENF-02).
- NODE-ARCH-15: Larger backends may split contexts into npm workspaces with explicit dependencies (ARCH-ENF-06).

## [Node.js Tooling](../08-crosscutting-concepts/development/node-tooling.md)

- NODE-TOOL-01: The Node version is the current Active LTS line, pinned in `backend/.nvmrc` (`26`) and in `package.json` `engines` (`"node": ">=26.13 <27"`, `"npm": ">=11.10.0"`), with `engine-strict=true` (TS-TOOL-14).
- NODE-TOOL-02: `tsconfig.json` uses the TS-TOOL-01 checks with Node settings:
- NODE-TOOL-03: Production runs compiled JavaScript.
- NODE-TOOL-04: ESLint uses the TS-TOOL-04 config (template: `.agents/skills/baseline-nestjs/templates/eslint.config.ts`, which contains every rule of NODE-TOOL-05), with ESLint 9:
- NODE-TOOL-05: Node backends add these rules to the shared set:
- NODE-TOOL-06: Prettier as in TS-TOOL-08 (`printWidth: 120`, `singleQuote`, `trailingComma: all`).
- NODE-TOOL-07: Every Node backend offers these script names (TS-TOOL-10 for backends):
- NODE-TOOL-08: TS-TOOL-11..16 apply unchanged.
- NODE-TOOL-09: Production dependencies are kept apart from dev dependencies.
- NODE-TOOL-10: `package.json` keeps `"version": "0.0.0"`.

## [TypeScript Tooling](../08-crosscutting-concepts/development/typescript-tooling.md)

- TS-TOOL-01: `strict` is on, plus these checks.
- TS-TOOL-02: The supported browsers are the Baseline "widely available" browsers of a date the baseline fixes, and `lib` is the newest ECMAScript level all of them support.
- TS-TOOL-03: No `any`.
- TS-TOOL-04: ESLint flat config with this plugin set:
- TS-TOOL-05: Lint errors fail the build. No warnings policy:
- TS-TOOL-06: Disabling a rule inline requires a named rule and a reason (`// eslint-disable-next-line rule -- reason`), enforced by `@eslint-community/eslint-comments/require-description` and `no-unlimited-disable`;
- TS-TOOL-07: Known overlaps are resolved in the shared config, not per project:
- TS-TOOL-08: Prettier formats everything it supports (TS, HTML templates, SCSS/CSS, JSON, Markdown, YAML).
- TS-TOOL-09: CI runs `prettier --check` and `eslint`.
- TS-TOOL-10: Every TypeScript project offers the same script names, so humans, agents and CI don't have to guess:
- TS-TOOL-11: `.npmrc` sets `ignore-scripts=true`, `allow-git=none` (or `root`) and `min-release-age=7` (days; SEC-CI-02), CI installs with `npm ci`, and `package-lock.json` is committed with its diffs reviewed.
- TS-TOOL-12: CI scans the lockfile for known vulnerabilities and runs `npm audit signatures`;
- TS-TOOL-13: Dependencies are added deliberately (age, maintainers, install scripts, usage checked).
- TS-TOOL-14: The toolchain guarantees an npm that knows the `.npmrc` keys.
- TS-TOOL-15: Dependency updates are automated as a capability of the repository.
- TS-TOOL-16: Builds are reproducible.
- TS-TOOL-17: knip reports unused dependencies, exports and files, and `verify` runs it.
- TS-TOOL-18: `check` is the inner loop, `verify` the gate.
- TS-TOOL-19: `verify` and `check` run every step, report all failures together and fail at the end.
- TS-TOOL-20: E2E code is type-checked and linted inside `verify`.
- TS-TOOL-21: ESLint bans reading the wall clock outside the platform clock (TS-ARCH-22).
